input.recap: The printer chat and the project chat use the same font at the same size. Both are the same web page with the same stylesheet: HarmonyOS Sans SC, 14 px on 20 px lines. I checked the code but did not measure the running app.
input.ask: Should the printer chat's text get bigger than the project chat's?

content.text:
Yes, it's the same font at the same size. The printer chat isn't a separate page. It's the same Agent web page as the project chat, loaded into the same kind of web view (`AgentWebView`), and it uses the same stylesheet, `AgentUI/src/styles.css`. Every chat message gets the body text style: HarmonyOS Sans SC at 14 px on 20 px lines. Nothing in the stylesheet changes the text size for the printer chat, and the C++ code doesn't zoom either web view. I checked this in the code only; I didn't measure the running app.

**What's smaller on purpose.** Some lines in your screenshot are one step below body text, and these are the same sizes used in the project chat:
- The "Tip: a photo is the fastest way…" line and "256 × 256 × 250 mm" are 12 px.
- "0.4 mm nozzle" in the "Added" card is 12 px too.

**Why it may still look small.** The two chats sit in different spaces:
- The project chat sits in a side pane about 429 px wide, on a light grey background.
- The printer chat takes over the whole workspace. It shows a column up to 720 px wide on the white canvas, with 16 px of padding around it.

The same 14 px text, set in long lines in a big white area, looks smaller than it does in a narrow pane, even though the pixels are the same. That last part is my guess about why it reads that way, not something I measured.

**Decision needed: should the printer chat use bigger text than the project chat?**
- **Keep it as is.** This costs nothing, and the two chats stay identical.
- **Make it bigger.** This would mean a new size in the design token file (the shared file of colours and sizes), for example 15 or 16 px for messages in the printer chat only. The project's design rules require that new size plus a test that checks it, so a size typed straight into the stylesheet isn't allowed. The cost is that the two chats would no longer match.
- **Narrow the column instead.** A third option is to shrink the printer chat's 720 px column so lines are shorter. That might fix how it feels without changing the text size.

My pick is to keep the size and try the narrower column first, but this is a design call for you to make. Which do you want?

Also, when the user is done adding a printer, we still get this pop up. It's really confusing. I think we have two options. The first is for, is to tell the agents to offer an option to end a conversation when it has successfully added a printer or connected the printer. The other option is just to tell the the agent to flag the session can be safely closed. I slightly prefer the first if we can reliably prompt agent to do so

Today the printer chat always asks before closing once the person has typed anything. In `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:549`, the Back button shows "Close this conversation?" whenever the chat has started, and it doesn't check whether the printer was already added. The agent's instructions (`printerInstructions.ts:170`) tell it to say "You can close this chat now" and also say "Do not add a Choices line." So the person reads that they can close, presses Back, and then gets a warning.

**Your first option was built before.** Until 2026-09-28 the agent ended its last reply with a "Done" button. When the person tapped it, the agent called a `printer_setup_finish` tool that closed the panel. Commit b60fc2d8e6 ("Remove dialog-only printer tools") removed both, and I found no recorded reason in the commit, the test README, or past sessions. On reliability, the old prompt tests passed most runs when checking that the agent offered Done in the four finished states: after declining to connect, after a verified connection, after leaving a failed connection, and after a nozzle change. Those tests used DeepSeek V4 Flash with 3 runs each, which is a small sample.

**What I'd propose (not built):** the agent again ends its finishing reply with a "Done" button, and the page handles the tap itself.
- Tapping Done closes the panel with no confirmation and no extra model call. The old design needed a second model round trip to call the close tool, and that step could fail. This version doesn't.
- The same button also works as your second option's "safe to close" flag. While the newest reply offers Done, Back closes without the confirmation too. One thing the agent writes covers both cases: tapping Done and pressing Back.
- If the agent forgets the button, the person sees today's behaviour, which is the confirmation.

**Decision needed: should the page offer Done this way, or skip the confirmation without asking the agent at all?**
- **Done button, as above.** You get the ending you prefer. It costs a prompt edit plus a run of the printer prompt test suite on the live model, and that run spends API credit, which needs your OK. It only works when the agent remembers the button.
- **Skip the confirmation after a successful add or connect.** The app already knows when either succeeds, so Back would close quietly from then on. Nothing depends on the model, and it needs no prompt change or live test. The person gets no Done button, only Back.

My pick is the Done button, because it's what you asked for and it fixes Back as well. If the live test shows the agent often forgets the button, I'd add the second option as a fallback.

Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. The same applies when the person says they're done.
